root_cause.text: The mlx5 RDMA driver registered its `MLX5_DEV_EVENT_SYS_ERROR` notifier too late and only on the LAG master path, so during firmware reset/unload in LAG mode the slave could die without the bond device receiving the fatal error event, leaving UMR completions never to arrive and causing an indefinite wait in `mlx5_ib_dereg_mr()`.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message says “In LAG mode the bond device is only registered on the master, so it never sees sys_error events from the slave” and that “UMR waits [hang] forever on unload as the slave is dead but the master hasn't entered error state yet”; the patch fixes this by adding a dedicated `sys_error` notifier stage “registered before `MLX5_IB_STAGE_IB_REG` and stays alive until after `ib_unregister_device()`,” and the diff moves `MLX5_DEV_EVENT_SYS_ERROR` handling out of `mlx5_ib_handle_event()` into a separate notifier/workqueue path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove an unused local variable from mlx5_ib_handle_event to clean up the code.
intent_record.what: The local variable `bool fatal = false;` was removed from `mlx5_ib_handle_event(struct work_struct *_work)`. No other code in the shown hunk was changed.
intent_record.how: This change has no runtime effect by itself in the shown diff, because the removed variable was only declared here and is not used elsewhere in the hunk. It likely eliminates an unused variable and may resolve a compiler warning.

intent_record.intent_summary: Stop mlx5_ib_handle_event() from treating MLX5_DEV_EVENT_SYS_ERROR as a device-fatal event in this path.
intent_record.what: Removed the case branch for MLX5_DEV_EVENT_SYS_ERROR from mlx5_ib_handle_event(), which previously set ibev.event to IB_EVENT_DEVICE_FATAL, called mlx5_ib_handle_internal_error(ibdev), assigned ibev.element.port_num from work->param, and set fatal = true.
intent_record.how: The handler no longer processes MLX5_DEV_EVENT_SYS_ERROR in this switch statement, so that event will not trigger the internal error handling or emit a device-fatal IB event from this code path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Stop `mlx5_ib_handle_event()` from clearing `ib_active` on fatal events.
intent_record.what: The two lines that set `ibdev->ib_active = false` when `fatal` is true were removed from `mlx5_ib_handle_event()`, leaving only the existing `ib_dispatch_event(&ibev)` path and the cleanup label.
intent_record.how: Fatal events no longer directly mark the IB device as inactive in this function, so the active state is preserved here instead of being cleared during event handling. Any deactivation now must happen through some other path or no longer occurs at this point.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add mlx5 sys-error notifier handling to propagate fatal device events and deactivate the IB device on system errors.
intent_record.what: Added a new sys-error event path for mlx5_ib: a workqueue handler that processes MLX5_DEV_EVENT_SYS_ERROR, calls mlx5_ib_handle_internal_error(), derives a port number from the notifier parameter, validates the port, optionally dispatches IB_EVENT_DEVICE_FATAL if the device is active, marks ib_active false, and frees the work item. Also added notifier callback registration and cleanup helpers to hook this handler into mlx5_notifier_register/unregister via dev->sys_error_events.
intent_record.how: When the underlying mlx5 device reports a system error, the driver now asynchronously handles it instead of ignoring it, converts it into an InfiniBand fatal device event for valid ports, and transitions the IB device to an inactive state. This improves error propagation and recovery by notifying upper layers that the device is no longer usable after a fatal system error.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add the system error notifier stage to the mlx5 IB profile so notifier setup and cleanup occur during device lifecycle management.
intent_record.what: A new profile stage entry was inserted into the `pf_profile` stage सूची: `MLX5_IB_STAGE_SYS_ERROR_NOTIFIER`, wired to `mlx5_ib_stage_sys_error_notifier_init` and `mlx5_ib_stage_sys_error_notifier_cleanup`, placed between the existing `MLX5_IB_STAGE_WHITELIST_UID` and `MLX5_IB_STAGE_IB_REG` stages.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the mlx5 IB profile will now run an additional initialization and cleanup step for the system error notifier during device setup and teardown, allowing notifier-related functionality to be established and later released as part of the staged lifecycle.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add system error notifier initialization and cleanup to the raw Ethernet profile stage sequence.
intent_record.what: A new stage entry named MLX5_IB_STAGE_SYS_ERROR_NOTIFIER was inserted into the raw_eth_profile stage list, using mlx5_ib_stage_sys_error_notifier_init as its init callback and mlx5_ib_stage_sys_error_notifier_cleanup as its cleanup callback, placed between the WHITELIST_UID and IB_REG stages.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the mlx5 IB profile will now initialize and later clean up the system error notifier stage as part of the profile bring-up/teardown sequence, enabling notifier setup that previously was not part of this profile's stage flow.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a new mlx5_ib stage for system error notifier handling.
intent_record.what: A new enum value, MLX5_IB_STAGE_SYS_ERROR_NOTIFIER, was inserted into the mlx5_ib_stages enumeration between MLX5_IB_STAGE_WHITELIST_UID and MLX5_IB_STAGE_IB_REG.
intent_record.how: This extends the ordered stage list with an additional initialization/registration stage, allowing the driver to track and execute a system error notifier step as part of its staged setup or teardown flow.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add per-device notifier storage for system error event handling.
intent_record.what: A new struct notifier_block field named `sys_error_events` was added to `struct mlx5_ib_dev`, alongside the existing `mdev_events` and `lag_events` members.
intent_record.how: This change expands the device state to register or track an additional notifier callback for system error events, enabling the driver to receive and handle that event stream at runtime.

consistency_review.core_intent: Prevent mlx5_ib_handle_event() from misclassifying MLX5_DEV_EVENT_SYS_ERROR as a fatal path that clears ib_active.
Add mlx5 system error notifier handling and integrate it into the IB profile lifecycle so fatal device events are propagated and notifier setup/cleanup happen during device management.
Add infrastructure for per-device system error notifier handling in mlx5_ib.

relevance_review.reason: The change only removes an unused local variable in mlx5_ib_handle_event and does not affect notifier registration timing, LAG master/slave event handling, or the sys error path that caused the hang.

The root cause is that the SYS_ERROR notifier was registered too late and only on the LAG master path, so the fatal event was not delivered during reset/unload in LAG mode. This group instead changes how mlx5_ib_handle_event() classifies SYS_ERROR and whether it clears ib_active, which is a different behavior change and does not address the notifier registration/timing issue.

The changes directly address the root cause by adding MLX5 system error notifier handling and moving notifier setup into the IB profile lifecycle, which would ensure fatal device events are propagated in time instead of being missed in LAG mode.

The root cause is that the MLX5 system error notifier was registered too late and only on the LAG master path. This change adds system error notifier initialization and cleanup earlier in the raw Ethernet profile stage sequence, which directly addresses the notifier timing/coverage problem involved in the hang.

The root cause is that the MLX5_DEV_EVENT_SYS_ERROR notifier was registered too late and only on the LAG master path, so the fatal error event could be missed. This group adds per-device system error notifier handling infrastructure in mlx5_ib, which directly addresses that notifier placement/coverage problem.

candidates.rationale: The root cause is that system-error notifier setup happened too late in the IB device lifecycle. This pre-fix stage sequence shows IB registration occurring before any dedicated device notifier stage existed, meaning fatal events could be missed during reset/unload in LAG mode.

The raw Ethernet profile had the same lifecycle ordering problem: IB registration was present without an earlier system-error notifier stage, so the driver could become active before fatal device events were being observed.

This is the per-device notifier storage used for event propagation. The vulnerability stems from notifier handling being absent or not properly integrated into the lifecycle, so fatal MLX5_DEV_EVENT_SYS_ERROR notifications were not delivered to the RDMA device in time.

vuln_statements.explanation: This pre-fix stage ordering registers the IB device without a dedicated earlier system-error notifier stage, which is the lifecycle bug that allowed MLX5_DEV_EVENT_SYS_ERROR to be missed during LAG reset/unload.

This per-device notifier storage is the field used to receive system error events; the vulnerability is tied to it not being properly integrated early enough into device lifecycle handling, so fatal events were not propagated in time.
